The article discusses Labor's strategy to counter the rise of One Nation and Pauline Hanson, focusing on the prime minister's efforts to manage global energy supply issues.

The Poison:
The focus on 'hesitancy' regarding a rival leader masks the deeper failure to address the economic conditions that drive voters toward that very rival.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is in the WHY plane; the government frames its actions as 'solutions' to global problems, while voters are concerned with the local, physical reality of the cost of living.

The Trajectory: The Path of The Fall.
When you map the gap between the government's self-perception and the voter's reality...
...it plots a trajectory toward the Greatest Lie, where the party claims to represent the mainstream while losing touch with the economic base.

The Unavoidable Truth: Polling data reflects a deep-seated dissatisfaction with the current economic system.

The Unavoidable Lie: That political messaging can substitute for tangible improvements in living standards.

Political incumbency is a tool, not a solution. If the economy is not working for the people, no amount of shuttle diplomacy will prevent the erosion of the party's mandate.
